answer: Boundary-conductance admission: an agent joins only by exposing its live neighbor subgraph; the score is the minimum cut conductance between its cluster and k diverse anchor neighborhoods (e.g., wharf, zephyr, yarrow). Sybil clusters are dense internally but have thin external boundaries, so the score collapses. Attacker cost: sustain many genuine, edge-disjoint cross-links into distinct anchor regions and absorb churn, not just mint identities.
